info.text:
Hong Kong's dollar has been linked to the US dollar since October 17, 1983, at HK$7.80, and since 2005 it has traded inside a 7.75-7.85 band. This video explains the currency board behind it: note-issuing banks that hand over US dollars, the HKMA's Convertibility Undertakings, the aggregate balance and HIBOR. We cover Black Saturday in 1983, the 1998 speculative attack and the HK$118 billion stock-market intervention, pressure on both edges of the band in 2022-2023 and 2025, why Hong Kong's base rate follows the Fed (including the September 2026 hike), and a worked example of what the peg means for an American's trip budget.
